reasoning_traces.think:
The ScoutGPT framework operates on a tokenized representation of football matches, where each event is encoded as a sequence of tokens including team identifiers, player roles, actions, and game state. The core mechanism uses a decoder-only transformer architecture (NanoGPT backbone) to predict the next token in the sequence, guided by two objectives: next-token prediction and goal-scoring outcome prediction. This dual-head setup allows the model to learn both syntactic and semantic structures of gameplay. During inference, constrained decoding ensures that ball possession and episode boundaries align with real-world game logic, preventing impossible or inconsistent sequences. For counterfactual simulations, the model swaps player tokens into a new team context and generates multiple Monte Carlo episodes to estimate residual value added (VAEP). This process enables GSE to simulate how a player might perform in different environments, while GSI applies Bayesian methods to refine estimates based on observed outcomes. The system's strength lies in its ability to generalize across diverse match situations through language-like abstraction, yet it suffers from limitations in handling rare or novel game states not present in training data.
